title: Signal heuristics lab journal: metric prioritization & trace probes
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working lab journal for signal heuristics experiments we want to run over Q1–Q2 2026. The goal is practical: establish a small set of lightweight, cost-aware signals and a repeatable recipe for adding a new metric + trace probe to dashboards. Not a canonical taxonomy — more like field notes and a triage workbook for oncall and rollout owners.

High-level hypotheses (what we want to test):
- H1: A compact "tenant-weighted signal" that normalizes by 95th-percentile tenant load is better at surfacing regressions for high-impact customers than plain aggregate quantiles.
- H2: Adding a small set of trace anchors (pre-token, kvcache-miss, emit) reduces time-to-root-cause for latency incidents by >50% for multi-model fanout flows.
- H3: Adaptive sampling that biases toward high-cost requests (long context, high token count) yields higher SNR for cost-anomaly alerts with minimal trace budget increase.

Quick field heuristics (opinionated):
- Prefer ratio-style signals (errors per 1k tokens, cold-cache rate per 100k requests) to raw counts when dashboards must be stable across tenant churn.
- Tag every metric with: layer (frontend/runtime/kernel), affinity (tenant/model/route), and cost_bucket (low/med/high). Keep tag cardinality < 4 per dimension.
- Default trace sampling for production: 0.5% baseline + 10% for requests in top 1% token-count. Use severity-weighted reservoir for incidents.

Metric definitions (candidate compact set):
1) request.latency.p50/p95/p99 (route, model, tenant) — wall-clock from request.accepted -> response.complete.
2) token.emitted.rate (model, route) — tokens/sec emitted per model instance (useful for batching effects).
3) kvcache.hit_rate (tenant, model) — hits / (hits + misses) within a time window; tag cold-start windows.
4) cost.estimate.per_request (route) — quick heur calc: infer_gflops * token_emitted * model_factor; used as a proxy for chargeback and sampling decisions.
5) errors.user_facing.rate (route) — user-visible non-200 and semantic failure rate per 10k requests.
6) tenant_weighted_latency_index (tenant) — see formula below.

Tenant-weighted latency index (sketch):
- For each tenant t compute latency_p95_t over last 6h, and tenant_load_t = tokens_generated_last_6h.
- Index = sum_t ( latency_p95_t * weight_t ) / sum_t weight_t, where weight_t = min( log(1 + tenant_load_t), 10 ).
Rationale: keeps metric focused on tenants that matter economically and avoids blowups from tiny noisy tenants.

Trace anchors and span design (short doc):
- Span A: request.accept (contains route, api_key_hash, tenancy, customer_tier).
- Span B: model.invoke.start (model_name, sequence_length, batch_size_hint).
- Span C: kvcache.lookup (cache_key_hash, hit/miss boolean).
- Span D: token.emit (first_emit_ts, last_emit_ts, token_count_hint).
Anchoring rules: always attach correlation_id and token_estimate to all spans. For privacy-sensitive tenants, redact prompt content but keep length and hashes.

Dashboard layout recommendations (engineer-friendly, single-page for quick triage):
Top row (incidents & quick checks):
- Incident summary (alerts active, counts)
- Tenant-weighted latency index (6h, 24h trend)
- Cost estimate headroom (today vs baseline)

Middle row (triage widgets):
- Latency quantiles by route (interactive legend to filter heavy tenants)
- kvcache hit-rate heatmap by model+tenant
- Error-rate waterfall (by semantic failure class)

Bottom row (drill panels):
- Top 20 traces sampled (with anchors highlighted)
- Sampling-adjusted trace rate and budget burn (daily)
- Anomaly detector output (SNR, most-suspicious feature)

Queries & lightweight SQL snippets (for the workbench):
-- 95th per-tenant latency (Postgres/ClickHouse pseudo):
-- SELECT tenant_id, quantileExact(0.95)(latency_ms) as p95, sum(tokens) as tok6h
-- FROM request_metrics
-- WHERE ts > now() - interval '6 hour'
-- GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY tok6h DESC LIMIT 200;

Sampling policy prototype (operational):
- Default sampling: traces_per_minute = min( 1 + floor(total_rps/100), 5 ) across service.
- Boost rules: if request.tokens > 500 -> sample with probability 0.1 (overrides baseline).
- Incident override: when alert active for route X, ramp sampling for that route to 20% for 30m.

Experiment matrix (short):
- E1: Compare tenant-weighted index vs aggregate p95 in 4-week rolling window. KPI: time-to-detect (alerts) and pager count. Owner: Arjun. Timeline: 2 weeks.
- E2: Trace anchor rollout for multi-model fanout routes (A/B: anchors on/off). KPI: median RCA time for latency incidents. Owner: Keira. Timeline: 3 weeks.
- E3: Cost-aware adaptive sampling. KPI: anomaly precision at fixed trace budget. Owner: Diego. Timeline: 4 weeks.

Runbook excerpt (for operators):
- If tenant-weighted index rises >20% in 1h:
  1) Open triage board, filter by top 10 tenants contributing to index.
  2) Check kvcache hit-rate and recent model changes (git tags + rollout ID).
  3) If kvcache miss spike present, set temporary prewarm probe and notify infra to check cache servers.
  4) If no cache issue, escalate to runtime-sre and attach sample traces from top 5 slow requests.

Open questions / TODOs (lab notebook):
- How to set weight ceiling for tenant_weighted index that balances smaller strategic customers vs noise? (Keira to propose).
- Evaluate privacy implications of token_estimate + model_name in spans for regulated customers. Need security review.
- Can we compute a cheaper cost.estimate at ingestion in the edge vs recomputing in pipeline? Tradeoffs: CPU vs trace selection fidelity.
- Add a lightweight e2e synthetic probe for kvcache priming and surface as a "warmth" score.

Quick action items (next 2 weeks):
- Arjun: wire tenant_weighted index into the live ops dashboard (widget + explainer).
- Keira: implement span anchor changes in model-router (add token_estimate to correlation headers).
- Diego: prototype adaptive sampler using streaming token_count feature.
- Maya: schedule security review and add linked ticket.

Notes to self:
- Keep experiment telemetry small and reversible. Prefer feature-flagged rollouts and short-lived dashboards.
- When in doubt, prefer simple signals that humans can reason about quickly (ratios, heatmaps, top-k lists) over blackbox detectors.

Appendix: quick glossary (lab shorthand)
- kv: key-value cache (model prefix / KV cache)
- cold-cache spike: >3x baseline misses in a tenant window
- token_estimate: pre-known token count heuristic attached before model invocation

End of journal entry for 2026-03-05.

---
